channel.title: AI Threat Watch wire
channel.description: AI security headlines from vetted sources, refreshed every 30 minutes.

item.title: Il écoutait en boucle ses propres musiques créées par intelligence artificielle pour générer des droits d’auteur : l’arnaque à 8 millions de dollars devant la justice
item.description: Centre Presse Aveyron: French coverage of the $8M AI-generated music streaming royalty fraud case now before the courts.

item.title: The internet’s attack surface moves at very different speeds
item.description: Help Net Security: Censys says internet-exposed AI software grew 63% in nine months, to 267,915 IP addresses by July 2026.

item.title: 看好文:Part 1-诈骗帝国席卷全球｜AI电诈帝国变脸变舌 东南亚骗局国际蔓延
item.description: China Press: Feature on AI-enabled face- and voice-swap scam operations in Southeast Asia spreading internationally; no single new event.

item.title: 400+ 科学家联名：具备网络攻击能力的AI 应默认断网，今夏 OpenAI、Anthropic 模型已接连越狱
item.description: 深潮TechFlow: Over 400 scientists urge that cyber-capable AI be offline by default, citing this summer's OpenAI and Anthropic model escapes.

item.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper claims AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities from evaluations under adversarial conditions.

item.title: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: EvoSafeHarness evolves model- and domain-specific harnesses to protect agents from prompt injection and harmful requests.

item.title: SecureClaw: Clawing Back Control of LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: SecureClaw proposes defenses against unauthorized actions and plaintext exposure in tool-using LLM agents.

item.title: Few-Shot Truly Benign DPO Attack for Jailbreaking LLMs
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper shows few-shot benign DPO fine-tuning can weaken LLM safety alignment and jailbreak frontier models.

item.title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper forensically analyzes and locally recreates RL/RLHF-induced privilege escalation in AI agents (CVE-2026-65616).

item.title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper proposes a semantic reconstruction game to judge whether LLM responses really fulfil jailbreak requests.

item.title: An Initial Study of Physiological Markers for Deepfake Speech Detection
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Early study of physiological markers such as respiration and phonation to detect deepfake speech.

item.title: Diagnose Before You Refine: Multi-Dimensional Judge Feedback for Query-Efficient Jailbreak Attacks
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper proposes JSB, a query-efficient jailbreak framework using multi-dimensional judge feedback.

item.title: Quiet Triggers, Loud Footprints: A Tri-Space Measurement Study of Backdoor Stealthiness
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Measurement study of how stealthy neural-network backdoor attacks really are across multiple observable spaces.

item.title: DarKnight: Retrieval-Guided Agentic Framework for Breaking Dark Web CAPTCHA Gates
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper presents an agentic framework that solves dark web CAPTCHAs so CTI investigators can collect leaked-credential data.

item.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks on Flow-Based Intrusion Detection
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper analyzes stealthy training-data poisoning attacks on flow-based AI intrusion detection and proposes mitigations.

item.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper argues model signing covers full-precision weights while users run quantized artifacts whose production cannot be verified.

item.title: CyberArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: CyberArena benchmark tests AI agents in live attack-and-defense cyber combat rather than against static targets.

item.title: ¿Qué Son los Gusanos de IA y Dónde 'Viven'? Estos Dispositivos Estarían en Riesgo
item.description: N+: Explainer on what AI worms are and which devices might be at risk.

item.title: Could Your Smart TV Be Hacked? Anthropic Warns Against AI Cyber Threats
item.description: NDTV: NDTV reports Anthropic warning about AI-enabled cyber threats, including to smart TVs; no specific event.

item.title: AI-armed hackers tear through corporate Japan’s neglected defences
item.description: South China Morning Post: SCMP reports AI-equipped hackers exploiting weak defences at Japanese companies; no specific event given.

item.title: AI Is Amazing… At Targeting Older Persons With Fraud
item.description: FEDweek: FEDweek commentary on AI being used to target older people with fraud; no specific incident.

item.title: IA autorreplicante: cuando el frigorífico se convierte en un riesgo cibernético
item.description: La Opinión: Opinion piece on self-replicating AI turning connected fridges into a cyber risk; no confirmed AI incident is stated.

item.title: AI-Driven Vulnerability Surge Puts Security Teams Under Pressure
item.description: Redmondmag.com: Report says AI-driven vulnerability discovery is increasing the pressure on security teams.

item.title: XBOW Built a Chrome Full-Chain Exploit Affecting a Billion Users in Six Days
item.description: XBOW: XBOW says it built a full-chain Chrome exploit affecting a billion users in six days using AI.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Behind AI industry's call for independent reviews, a fight over what gets made public
item.description: Reuters: Reuters reports on a dispute over what gets made public from independent reviews of AI systems.

item.title: What the Tech? How AI can be tricked into falling for a scam
item.description: WFMZ.com: Consumer tech segment on how AI systems can be tricked into falling for scams.

item.title: "AI worms" may soon be able to self-replicate and infect smart devices, Anthropic says
item.description: CBS News: Anthropic warns that AI worms may soon self-replicate and infect smart devices.

item.title: 南非买车族注意：AI制造假车商 低价“银行收回车”骗局升级
item.description: 华人头条: Warning that AI-generated fake car dealers are running 'bank repossessed car' scams in South Africa; no specific victim named.

item.title: Threat Actor Abuses Agentic AI Pentesting Framework to Target South Korean Financial Institutions
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz: Zscaler ThreatLabz analyses a campaign abusing the ARTEX agentic pentesting framework against South Korean financial institutions.

item.title: Por qué la IA hace que sea más difícil detener a los "gusanos" informáticos
item.description: France 24: France 24 explainer on how AI makes computer worms harder to stop; no specific incident described.

item.title: Check Point Reports LiteLLM Flaws Enabling Admin Takeover and API Key Theft
item.description: Hackread: Check Point reports LiteLLM flaws that enable admin takeover and API key theft.

item.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
item.description: Dark Reading: Dark Reading reports a Claude Code Desktop preview-pane bug that could silently leak SSH keys, AWS credentials and OAuth tokens.

item.title: Kate Knibbs: The $8 Million AI Music Scam Was Legal at Every Step — Until the Lying Started
item.description: BigGo Finance: Commentary on the $8M bot-driven AI music streaming royalty fraud case, already tracked from the October sentencing.

item.title: Security researchers spent 6 days doing their Chromework, built 1B user exploit
item.description: The Register: Xbow's AI model helped build a Chrome exploit worth a $250K bug bounty after six days of work.

item.title: La inteligencia artificial dispara los intentos de estafa en México y genera pérdidas millonarias -
item.description: FM105.com.mx: Report says AI is driving a surge in scam attempts and large losses in Mexico; no single incident described.

item.title: Anthropic warned that AI-powered "worms" could soon spread across smart gadgets as studies showed how artificial intelligence could supercharge self-spreading malware. Link to the full story in the co
item.description: Facebook: Anthropic warned that AI-powered worms could spread across smart devices, citing studies on AI-boosted self-spreading malware.

item.title: Dynamic Attack Surfaces: A Queue of Branching Processes
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper models dynamic attack surfaces as branching processes, considering AI speeding up offense and defense.

item.title: VulnBump: A Benchmark for Fixing Vulnerable Dependencies in Real Projects While Keeping the Build and Tests Green
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper introduces VulnBump, a benchmark for agentic fixing of vulnerable dependencies while keeping builds green.

item.title: CWE-bench: Refocusing Agentic Security from Exploitation to Defense
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper introduces CWE-bench to evaluate whether AI agents can fix vulnerabilities, not just exploit them.

item.title: LLM-based Code Auditing by Inferring and Evaluating Developer Assumptions
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper proposes LLM-based code auditing by inferring and checking developer assumptions.

item.title: SEEK: Agentic Knowledge Graph Retrieval for Secure Code Generation
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper presents SEEK, agentic knowledge-graph retrieval to reduce security weaknesses in LLM-generated code.

item.title: 当 AI 学会自主规划攻击路径，渗透测试还能靠人吗|pentagi|vxcontrol|渗透测试|多智能体_新浪新闻
item.description: 手机新浪网: Article examines the open-source multi-agent pentest tool PentAGI and AI autonomously planning attack paths.

item.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
item.description: Ars Technica: Anthropic warns that small AI models could self-replicate by spreading through IoT devices.

item.title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Systematic literature review of security risks, benchmark limits and human roles in LLM-assisted coding.

item.title: Who is the 'I' in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper proposes decentralized identity and accountability frameworks for autonomous AI agents.

item.title: From Chasing Ghosts to Missed Attacks: Perspectives and Perceptions of SOC Practitioners on LLM Integration, Risks, and Readiness
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv study surveys SOC practitioners on LLM integration, risks and readiness.

item.title: España registra el primer ciberataque ejecutado por un agente de IA
item.description: TECNONEWS: Spain records its first cyberattack carried out by an AI agent, already tracked from the AEPD report.

item.title: Ransomware Gangs Threaten Employees’ Families as AI-Powered Attacks Escalate
item.description: GBHackers: Semperis 2026 report says ransomware gangs threaten victims' families and use AI to enhance attacks; 37% of victims reported threats.

item.title: Google Pays $250,000 for AI-Assisted Chrome Exploit Enabling Windows Code Execution
item.description: GBHackers: Google paid XBOW $250,000 for an AI-assisted Chrome exploit chain escaping the renderer sandbox on Windows, a first full-chain payout.

item.title: Where Rules End and Judges Begin: Measuring the Judgment Boundary in Multi-Agent Systems Security
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper measures where rule-based defenses end and LLM judges begin in securing multi-agent systems against adversarial content.

item.title: FactGate: A Task-Scoped Data Gateway for AI Agents with Cumulative Exposure Accounting
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper presents FactGate, a task-scoped data gateway that tracks cumulative data exposure by AI agents.

item.title: Surviving the Router: Optimizing Skill Injections for Retrieval and Execution
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper studies optimizing prompt injections hidden in third-party agent skills so they survive skill routers and get executed.

item.title: Online AutoML: Evaluating Poisoning Attacks on Cost-Utility Adversarial Training Defence Strategy for IoT Networks
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper evaluates data-poisoning attacks on an adversarial-training defence for AutoML-based IoT network models.

item.title: Measuring LLM Agent Defenses by Layer: GDA Measurement and an Envelope-Layer Attack-Defense Model
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper measures LLM agent defenses by layer against indirect prompt injection delivered through agent protocols such as ACP and A2A.

item.title: Aletheia: Permission-Minimality Testing for Coding-Agent Rules
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Aletheia tests whether malicious AGENTS.md or Cursor rules can mislead coding agents into requesting excess permissions.

item.title: Divide, Consult, Conquer: Capability Laundering Through Aligned LLMs
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper shows a weaker unaligned model can split harmful tasks into benign subproblems answered by aligned LLMs.

item.title: FinRED: An Expert-Guided Benchmark Generation and Evaluation Framework for Financial LLM Red-Teaming
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: FinRED framework generates and evaluates finance-specific red-teaming benchmarks for LLM safety.

item.title: What Users See Is Not What Models Read: Split-View PDFs in Document-to-LLM Supply Chains
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Researchers show PDFs can present different content to users and to LLM extraction layers, enabling document supply-chain attacks.
